text:
marie: Heads up — noticed a sudden spike in admin/grant operations from svc-batch-runner across prod. Looks like KMS grants + role changes combined. filing here as a triage thread, attaching quick audit snippet. cc @alex @raj

alex: on it. timeframe? any user-facing incidents? :eyes:

marie: saw spike 03/18 02:14–02:22 UTC, ~120 grant ops. No user incidents reported, but a downstream job failed with permission denied earlier (might be related). logs excerpt below:

marie: ```
2026-03-18T02:14:03Z audit: grant KMSKeyAccess principal=svc-batch-runner@proj-prod-42 reason=auto-rollout token_id=tok-9a3f
2026-03-18T02:14:15Z iam: attach-role role=admin:write principal=svc-batch-runner@proj-prod-42 performed_by=svc-deployer@infra
2026-03-18T02:14:47Z audit: grant KMSKeyAccess principal=svc-batch-runner@proj-prod-17 reason=manual-escalation token_id=tok-4b1c
```

raj: hmm. two different principals doing role attachments — svc-deployer and a manual escalation. can you paste the token issuer or Okta session id from the logs?

marie: token ids above, i pulled the okta audit id 0a1b2c in the longer logs. There's a matching okta session: okta_session=ss-77e4. Also found an associated PR in infra repos: github.com/redwood/infra/pull/512 -> looks like a deploy tool change that touched permissions.

lisa: tagging infra and devex: @eli @sam — any recent deploy-tool change that could've widened scopes?

eli: that PR is the one that added parallel job runners and added a helper to request temporary KMS grants during deploys. It should have used least-privilege scopes but i need to check the rollout flags.

sam: quick note — the helper calls back to the grant service which requires a justifier header. we added a fallback earlier for legacy callers that defaulted to a broader grant. i think that fallback was enabled in the 512 rollout.

alex: this smells like a regression from the fallback. can eng-security confirm whether token tok-9a3f was minted by service account or by human? if by service, we need to check who authorized fallback.

audits-bot: RECONCILE: token tok-9a3f -> issuer=svc-deployer@infra (service principal), okta_session=SSN-N/A, justification="auto-rollout". tok-4b1c -> issuer=eli (human), okta_session=ss-77e4, justification="manual-escalation".

raj: thanks bot. action plan suggestion: 1) revoke remaining active grants for svc-batch-runner across affected projects 2) block the fallback path in grant service immediately 3) roll back PR 512 or toggle canary off 4) add this incident evidence to quarterly access review and mark for least-privilege audit.

marie: +1 to plan. i've started revocations for proj-42 and proj-17 — will post results in a sec.

marie: revocation results: ```
revoke KMSKeyAccess principal=svc-batch-runner@proj-prod-42 status=ok time=02:28
revoke KMSKeyAccess principal=svc-batch-runner@proj-prod-17 status=ok time=02:30
```

eli: i've toggled the fallback off and created an emergency patch to require explicit justifier header. pushing to canary now.

sam: rolling back PR 512 in infra. noting postmortem link: https://github.com/redwood/infra/issues/878

alex: i'll open a lightweight incident report and evidence bundle. need timeline, who approved, and whether this bypassed existing RBAC guards. also want to add KMS-grant telemetry to the access-review dataset (so quarterly review picks up spikes).

raj: agree. add this to the recurring least-privilege audit action items. recommend we: - instrument grant-service to emit aggregated deltas per principal per hour - add an alert when admin role attachments > 5/hr for any non-human principal - add KMS grants to owner-proof checks for resources with >3 principals

lisa: ok to me. we should also do a targeted access-review for svc-batch-runner's scope across org (owner/prj/editor flags). can we include the results in next week's security sync?

marie: yes — i'll prepare a short evidence package (okta session, PR diff, grant-service traces) and drop into the drive + incident doc.

eli: quick note on remediation: we'll add a hard stop in grant-service that rejects fallback unless explicitly approved via a tiered flow. also prepping a one-time manual justification roll-forward for safe rollouts.

sam: looping in product-security to confirm if any compliance boundaries were crossed. @lisa can you escalate to compliance?

lisa: done. i've pinged compliance and they want a copy of the evidence and timeline.

alex: thanks everyone. immediate owners: eli (fix grant-service), sam (rollback verification), marie (evidence + revocations), raj (alerts + audit dataset). i'll put together incident-00042 and assign follow-ups.

marie: putting quarterly-access-review tag on the incident and assigning the least-privilege audit item. thanks all. :thumbsup:

sam: follow-up question — do we want to include this svc principal in the admin-entitlement cleanup sweep next quarter? could be a candidate for narrowing or converting to more limited cross-project reader role.

raj: yes, add to the prune queue. mark ownerproof required and schedule a handback if no business case is found.

marie: closing triage for now. we'll keep thread updated if rollout flags flip or more artifacts surface.
